docs.summary: When true, every canvas lays out and maps to world using its **world-space** representation ([`ReferenceResolution`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.GameCanvas~ReferenceResolution) as the root rect + the GameObject transform), regardless of its actual [`RenderMode`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.RenderMode). The scene view enables this so screen-space UI can be viewed and edited in world space like any other GameObject, independent of screen/RT size.
The rendering mode of this GameCanvas.
Global scale factor applied to all elements.
Sort order relative to other screen-space canvases. Higher = on top.

Shared [`Material`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Material) using the `Default/DefaultUI` shader. Lazy-allocated; reused across every UI element that doesn't override [`GetMaterial`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.UIBehaviour~GetMaterial).

Shared [`Material`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Material) using the `Default/DefaultText` shader, which reconstructs sharp coverage from the single-channel SDF glyph atlas. Reused by every text element (UI `TextComponent` and the 3D `TextMeshComponent`) that doesn't override its material.

Called by descendants (or by the property setters above) to request a rebuild. The canvas rebuild is all-or-nothing: Layout and Hierarchy both need the full walk, and Vertices/Material are already tracked per element ([`DirtyFlags`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.UIBehaviour)), so the flags are only carried for the elements' benefit and not accumulated here.
Ensures this GameCanvas's GameObject and all descendants use RectTransform.
Called when the object becomes enabled and active. Only called when the GameObject is in a Scene and enabled.
Called when the object becomes disabled or inactive. Only called when the GameObject was in a Scene and becomes disabled.

Walks the hierarchy under this canvas, computes layout, generates meshes for any [`UIBehaviour`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.UIBehaviour) with dirty vertices, and produces a fresh `Tree`. Cheap when `_isDirty` is false (single boolean check + return).

Base canvas -> world transform without per-element pivot / rotation / scale. Per-mode: - WorldSpace -> [`LocalToWorldMatrix`](#api~Prowl.Vector.Transform~LocalToWorldMatrix) (design pixels map 1:1 to world units) - ScreenSpaceOverlay -> scale([`ScaleFactor`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.GameCanvas~ScaleFactor))
